Graph-Based Optimization of Sentinel-1 SBAS Interferometric Networks for Multi-Environment Deformation Monitoring

This repository accompanies the manuscript:

Graph-Based Optimization of Sentinel-1 SBAS Interferometric Networks for
Multi-Environment Deformation Monitoring

The repository contains the Python implementation of the proposed
graph-based redundancy-controlled SBAS network optimization framework
developed using the open-source PyGMTSAR environment.

================================================================================

SBASOptimized/
├── Beijing_Airport/ │ ├── Ascending/ │ └── Descending/

│ └── Processing utilities

================================================================================
SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS
================================================================================

Operating System - Linux (recommended) - macOS - Windows (WSL
recommended)

Python - Python 3.10+

External Software - GMTSAR - SNAPHU - Earthdata Login - ASF Download API

Python Dependencies - pygmtsar - xarray - numpy - pandas - geopandas -
matplotlib - pyvista - panel - dask - distributed - asf_search - json -
platform - os - sys - warnings - contextlib

================================================================================
COMMON PROCESSING PARAMETERS
================================================================================

-   SAR Dataset: Sentinel-1 SLC
-   Acquisition Mode: IW
-   Polarization: VV
-   DEM: NASA SRTM 1 arc-second
-   Temporal Baseline: 60 days
-   Maximum Perpendicular Baseline: ~150 m
-   Network Optimization: Graph-based redundancy-controlled pair
    selection
-   Redundancy Limit: 2
-   Iterations: 3
-   Phase Filtering: Persistent Scatterer Function weighting
-   Phase Unwrapping: SNAPHU
-   Time-Series Inversion: Coherence-weighted least squares
-   Velocity Estimation: Linear SBAS velocity
-   Parallel Computing: Dask

================================================================================
PROCESSING WORKFLOW
================================================================================

1.  Sentinel-1 burst selection
2.  ASF download
3.  Orbit download
4.  DEM download
5.  Scene alignment
6.  Geocoding
7.  Baseline generation
8.  Candidate interferogram generation
9.  Graph optimization
10. Persistent scatterer computation
11. Interferogram generation
12. SNAPHU phase unwrapping
13. Trend correction
14. SBAS inversion
15. LOS displacement
16. Velocity estimation

================================================================================
OUTPUT PRODUCTS
================================================================================

-   Candidate interferometric pair table
-   Optimized interferometric pair table
-   Graph diagnostics
-   LOS displacement
-   LOS velocity
-   Vertical displacement (dual orbit)
-   East-West displacement (dual orbit)
-   Point-of-interest time series
-   Runtime statistics
-   NetCDF output products

================================================================================
DATA AVAILABILITY
================================================================================

Sentinel-1 SLC bursts and precise orbit files are publicly available
through the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) Distributed Active Archive
Center (DAAC):

https://doi.org/10.5067/8W33RRS6S2RV

The processing scripts include the filtering criteria required to
retrieve the appropriate Sentinel-1 datasets for each study area.
